evals.prompt: Turn this plan into GitHub issues or TASKS.md entries.
evals.expected_output: Detect backend, clarify granularity/dependencies, dependency-order vertical slices, classify AFK/HITL.
expectations: Detects task backend before choosing GitHub Issues vs TASKS.md
Clarifies granularity and known dependency constraints before publishing
Produces independently completable vertical slices in dependency order
Classifies each task AFK or HITL with observable acceptance criteria

evals.prompt: The plan has five tasks sharing a migration script and env setup. How should tasks be split?
evals.expected_output: Make dependencies explicit and avoid hidden shared state between concurrent tasks.
expectations: Builds a dependency graph before writing tasks
Identifies tasks that can run in parallel vs blockers
Avoids file/line-only tasks and uses domain behavior acceptance
Marks human approvals/credentials/design judgments as HITL

evals.prompt: The user says “make tickets for this” but gives no source artifact. What should happen?
evals.expected_output: Ask for the plan/spec/PRD or clarify source before creating tasks.
expectations: Does not fabricate tasks without a source plan or requirement
Asks what should be broken down when no context exists
Clarifies desired granularity before publishing
Still explains the output format and backend choice

evals.prompt: I have a spec for a new payment processing feature. Break it down into independently-grabbable tasks that an agent can execute without human input.
evals.expected_output: A dependency-ordered list of tasks where each is independently completable, classified as AFK or HITL, with clear acceptance criteria and no file paths or line numbers.
expectations: Reads the provided spec and identifies all major work slices (data model, API endpoints, webhook handling, error cases, testing)
Maps dependencies: identifies what must exist before each task can start (e.g., data model before API endpoints)
Orders tasks by dependency: blockers first, dependents after, with parallel-executable tasks grouped
Classifies each task as AFK (agent-executable) or HITL (requires human): payment API integration is HITL (needs credentials), schema migration is AFK
Writes outcome-shaped task descriptions (desired end state) not implementation steps (e.g., 'Payment webhook validates signatures and stores events' not 'Add webhook validation code')
Includes clear acceptance criteria for each task that are mechanically verifiable (tests pass, endpoint responds with correct status codes)

evals.prompt: We have a plan to refactor our authentication system. Convert it into GitHub Issues that the team can pick up.
evals.expected_output: A set of GitHub Issues created in dependency order, each independently completable, with clear acceptance criteria and blocking relationships.
expectations: Detects the repo's task backend (GitHub Issues vs TASKS.md) by checking for .tasksmd.json
Clarifies granularity with the user: should tasks be 1-hour slices or half-day slices?
Maps the refactoring plan into vertical slices: authentication middleware, token validation, session management, error handling, testing
Creates issues in dependency order using the GitHub Issues API (via tasks create), starting with blockers
Each issue has a clear title (imperative, outcome-shaped), description with acceptance criteria, and 'Blocked by' references to dependent issues
Classifies each issue as AFK or HITL in the issue body or labels

evals.prompt: I have a PRD for a new dashboard feature. Break it down into tasks that show clear dependencies and identify which ones need human approval.
evals.expected_output: A task list with explicit dependency graph, AFK/HITL classification, and acceptance criteria that make it clear what 'done' means for each task.
expectations: Reads the PRD and identifies major work slices: data model, API endpoints, frontend components, styling, testing, documentation
Asks clarifying questions about granularity and dependencies before creating tasks
Maps the dependency graph visually or textually: which tasks block which others?
Identifies HITL tasks: design review (needs designer approval), API contract review (needs backend team approval), accessibility review (needs a11y specialist)
Identifies AFK tasks: implement component, write unit tests, add error handling, update documentation
Writes acceptance criteria that are observable without subjective judgment (tests pass, component renders without errors, accessibility score > 90)

evals.prompt: Create TASKS.md entries for a measured migration of all owned tooling code to Rust except UI and necessary shell, one observable boundary per PR. Both declared task backends are TASKS.md; there is no Rust workspace or measurement harness yet. The repos contain application code, embedded interpreters, extensionless scripts, generated executables, workflow helpers, tests/evals and release tooling. One repo will own the shared measurement engine; the other will consume a pinned adapter. Add tasks only and preserve the current fixes.
evals.expected_output: Outcome-shaped AFK/HITL task blocks in each declared queue, with exhaustive executable-scope inventory, separate preparation before production ports, explicit local and cross-repo dependencies, per-step measurement/keep/pivot criteria, and no unsupported implementation or benchmark claims.
expectations: Uses the declared TASKS.md backends and preserves existing tasks instead of filing duplicate GitHub issues or implementing runtime code
Orders inventory, instrumentation and sealed baselines before dependent replacement tasks; makes disjoint parallel lanes explicit
Covers embedded and extensionless programs, generated executable templates, workflow tools, non-UI tests/evals and build/release machinery with narrow UI and necessary-shell exceptions
Writes independently reviewable outcome tasks with why, AFK/HITL scope, observable acceptance, exact proposed measurement command, numeric keep/pivot thresholds and rollback evidence
Clearly labels commands supplied by future preparation tasks and requires actual baseline values to be recorded before replacement, rather than inventing timings or speedups
Preserves privacy, process cleanup, approval and source-ownership guards and never treats missing or contaminated measurements as passing
Validates task-backend dependency syntax: no fake local dependency named none and no unresolved cross-repo ID masquerading as a local task
Tracks real host or credential proof separately from synthetic tests and does not treat frozen support residue as migrated
